findings.now: Your gut barrier needs a lot of energy, to keep its tight junctions intact. If the cells lining your small intestine (called enterocytes) or the colonocytes lining your large intestine don't do that, the barrier loosens up.
findings.published: Your gut barrier requires massive amounts of immediate, localized energy to maintain tight junction integrity. If your enterocytes (small intestine) or colonocytes (large intestine) lack their preferred mitochondrial fuels, the barrier structurally collapses, allowing lipopolysaccharides (LPS) and endotoxins to leak into systemic circulation.
findings.why: "don't do that" most naturally points back to "keep its tight junctions intact," which turns the sentence into a circle (if the junctions aren't kept intact, the barrier loosens), and it loses the published condition that the cells are short of their preferred fuels.
where: Some Causes of poor gut health, P19

findings.now: Besides feeding the colonocytes, SCFAs lock down the barrier in your lower gut, preventing the dangerous escape of substances from gut to blood, which then turns down inflammatory signals that would be needed otherwise to contain the damage.
findings.published: Getting these via raw resistant starch fermentation or your home-brewed SIBO yogurt fuels colonocytes, locks down the lower gut barrier, and systematically suppresses inflammatory signals.
findings.why: The trailing "which then turns down inflammatory signals that would be needed otherwise" is hard to attach and has awkward word order, so a reader has to reread it to see that less leakage means less inflammation is needed.
where: Some Causes of poor gut health, P23

findings.now: Some people will tell you to take malic and citric acid (which make green apples and tart cherries sour) as an extra quick energy source for your enterocytes.
findings.published: TCA Cycle Intermediates (Malic & Citric Acid): Organic acids like malate and citrate feed directly into the exact same mitochondrial energy pathways as glutamine. Consuming clean, sour profiles—such as organic malic acid, tart cherries, or green apples—provides rapid, alternative fuel to gut epithelial cells, accelerating mucosal healing from a different biochemical angle.
findings.why: The published text recommended sour acids outright as an alternative fuel that speeds up healing of the gut lining, but NOW passes the advice on as what "some people" say, drops the healing claim and moves the reason for eating something sour to iron absorption, so the point has changed (flag it unless this change was approved).
where: Some Causes of poor gut health, P24

findings.now: And they do supply quick energy, because they are made and used by that mitochondrial energy cycle, also called the TCA or Krebs cycle. But glutamine is still the main thing they need, because it helps build new cells in addition to giving the needed energy.
findings.published: Organic acids like malate and citrate feed directly into the exact same mitochondrial energy pathways as glutamine.
